summary: Rajesh P. N. Rao works in computational fields and Indology. He studied at Angelo State University and the University of Rochester under Dana H. Ballard (~1993–1998), becoming a Professor of Computer Science at the University of Washington in 2000.

Rajkrishna Mukhopadhyay was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at Krishnagar Government College and Presidency University, later holding posts at Scottish Church College and Presidency University.

Working in Indology and history/archaeology, Raju Rimal studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus, Tribhuvan University, and the Norwegian University of Life Sciences. He was a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Oslo (2020–2024) and joined the Norwegian School of Sport Sciences in 2025.

Rakhal Das Banerji worked in Indology and archaeology, studying at Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, and under John Marshall. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1926) and was a professor at Banaras Hindu University (1928–1930).
Rakra Tethong Rinpoche studied under Trijang Rinpoche and Gendun Chopel.

Tibetologist Ralf Kramer studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and at the University of London. He has served as Tibetan librarian at the Indian Institute, Oxford, and as Aris Librarian at the Bodleian Library.

Working in philosophy and other fields, Ralph Abraham studied at the University of Michigan and under Debabrata Sensharma. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Columbia, and Princeton before serving as associate professor (1968) and professor (1980) at UC Santa Cruz.
Ralph Lerner is a philosopher who studied at the University of Chicago under Leo Strauss from around 1948 to 1953. He later held a post at the University of Chicago around 1959.

Indologist and linguist Ralph Lilley Turner studied at Christ's College, Cambridge, under Edward James Rapson and W. H. D. Rouse. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University and served as Director of SOAS University of London (1922–1957).

Indologist Ralph T. H. Griffith studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, under Horace Hayman Wilson. He became Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford in 1849 and served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1861 to 1878.
Working in philosophy and other fields, Ralph Waldo Emerson completed his education at Harvard College and Harvard Divinity School between 1817 and 1826.

Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Raluwe Padmasiri became a professor at the University of Kelaniya in 2012 and is attested as a professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies in 2026.
Ram Chandra Dhungana, active in Indology and history/archaeology, served as assistant editor for Ancient Nepal (attested 1973) and for the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1974).

Indologist and archaeologist Ram Chandra Kak studied at Sri Pratap College and trained under John Marshall. He served as Director of Jammu and Kashmir's Department of Archaeology and Research (1919–1929) and curator of Sri Pratap Singh Museum (~1919–1930).

Ram Chandra Pandeya was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale and T. R. V. Murti. At the University of Delhi, he headed Buddhist Studies (~1964–1973) and served as acharya (~1973–1997).

Indologist and linguist Ram Karan Sharma earned his PhD at UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He served as vice chancellor at Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1974–1980) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1984–1985).

Active in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, Ram Mohan Roy founded institutions including Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency University (1816), Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Mirat-ul-Akhbar (1822), Vedanta College (1826), Calcutta Unitarian Committee, and Brahmo Samaj (1828).

Ram Niwas Pandey works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology under doctoral supervisor Hit Narayan Jha.

Indologist and linguist Ram Prasad Bhatt studied at Hemwati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University (2003–2006). He was a lecturer and research associate at the University of Leipzig (2002–2003) before joining the University of Hamburg in 2003.
Indologist and philosopher Ram Shankar Bhattacharya studied under Raghunatha Shastri. He held positions at Tikmani Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya, the All-India Kashiraj Trust, and Banaras Hindu University.
